title: Product Engineer
description: 📈 Who We Are: We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair. We're rebuilding how energy is bought and sold. That means cutting out middlemen, connecting businesses directly with renewable generators, and ensuring every transaction is traceable and transparent . We're a 180+ person team - operators, data scientists, engineers, customer champions and energy experts - backed by top-tier investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Hitachi Ventures, Allianz, AlbionVC and Atomico. We closed a $75M Series B round in early 2026, taking our total funding to $94M, and we now power energy for over 4,000 UK businesses across 8,500+ sites , with over £75m in value returned to businesses and generators so far. We're a technology company solving the energy industry, not an energy company. Some people call us a neo-utility, the neo-bank idea, applied to energy. The industry is noticing. We were crowned Europe's Most Exciting Tech Company at the GP Bullhound Allstars awards , came in at #6 on LinkedIn's Top Startups 2026 in the UK, #7 on the Scaling Europe 50 of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and #14 on Sifted's AI 100 . Learn more about us on our website . 🚀 The Role We're hiring Product Engineers at Staff, Senior Staff, and Principal level across three of our engines: Buy, Sell and Third Party Access (TPA). A Product Engineer at tem gets handed a problem, not a ticket. You sit inside an engine, next to the account managers, partners and customers who live with the problem. You work out what to build, build it, and stay with it after launch until you can show it moved the metric. Product sets the bet and the guidance, not the feature list, so nobody writes your tickets for you. This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not a people-management one. We will talk to you about which engine fits you best, and where your experience and interests line up. Buy: Buy is where businesses pay less for clean power. It's the side of tem that runs RED for the UK businesses on it: quotes with every cost up front, bills itemised line by line, and a switch from quote to live in minutes, not days. You'd build the products and systems behind that, from tender to signed contract to a bill with nothing to hide, and make it work just as well for the next thousand sites as it does for the first. Sell: Sell is where generators earn more for what they produce. We contract with UK solar, wind, hydro, anaerobic digestion, biomass and EfW sites, from single farms to multi-site portfolios, through broker partners and direct. You'd build the tools that get generators signed faster, show them exactly what they're earning, and get them paid on time, every time. You'd also open up new kinds of sites we can't contract today, so there's more clean power to put in front of businesses. Third Party Access (TPA): TPA builds the new transaction rails for our partners. It lets brokers, banks, affiliates and generators sell tem's energy under their own brand, running on Rosso, our pricing engine. You'd design and build the partner APIs, branded portals, billing and settlement that make that work, and take a 0 to 1 product from pilot to production. In TPA you'll also be partner-facing, embedding with partners to get them integrated and live. 📆 In your first 12 months, you might: Sit with the account managers, partners and customers in your engine, run discovery calls yourself and turn what you hear into a clear problem to solve. Decide what to build and what to leave out, then design and ship it without waiting for a spec. Ship work that moves a named business metric, and stay with it until you can show the number moved. In TPA, help take partner integrations from pilot to production, live and working. Mentor engineers around you and share what you learn with teams across the business. 🛠️ Responsibilities Own discovery: Work directly with the commercial team, partners and customers to find the real problem, proactively engaging them and running calls autonomously. Turn problems into outcomes: Turn subjective requirements into objective outcomes, deciding what to build, then designing and shipping it yourself. Be accountable for the number: Take full accountability for the business and user metrics that move as a direct result of your technical and customer work. Own it end to end: Stay with it after launch and make sure it moves what it was meant to move within the business. Make the hard calls: Make sound but critical judgement calls on speed versus robustness, and on commercial risk. Spread what you learn: Feed what you learn from partners and customers back into the product, with an impact across departments that aren't your own. Raise the bar: Mentor engineers around you and raise technical standards, helping others accelerate into roles you used to hold. ✅ Requirements Must-Haves Proven technical leadership at Senior, Staff or Senior Staff level, with genuine, statistical evidence of leading complex, ambiguous work to real business impact. Comfort operating without a spec, with several clear-cut examples of how you went against the status quo or ran without guidelines to deliver something impactful. Examples of talking directly to customers and commercial teams to find the real problem, participating in (if not leading) early discovery calls and user feedback interviews. Sound commercial judgement, including an understanding of the revenue impact of the risks you take and whether a headcount investment outweighs its costs. Comfort being the technical voice in front of commercial stakeholders and partners, from our leadership team through to our board members and investors. A hands-on, player-coach approach, and comfort in our stack: Python, TypeScript, AWS serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, EventBridge) and event-driven architectures.
